title: Impact of High Thoracic Paravertebral Block on Diaphragmatic Function: a Prospective Study
official: Impact of High Thoracic Paravertebral Block on Diaphragmatic Function: a Prospective Study
summary: The high thoracic paravertebral block is a regional anesthesia technique commonly used for oncologic breast surgery. Local anesthetic is injected into the paravertebral space to provide anesthesia and pain relief. Case reports suggest that cephalad spread of local anesthetic may occasionally affect the phrenic nerve and lead to temporary hemidiaphragmatic dysfunction, but the incidence of this complication is unknown. The goal of this prospective interventional study is to evaluate the impact of high thoracic paravertebral block on diaphragmatic function in patients undergoing unilateral oncologic breast surgery. Diaphragmatic function will be assessed using ultrasound before and after the block. The study will also evaluate postoperative pain, opioid consumption, respiratory symptoms, and other postoperative outcomes.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Fully consented, ASA 1-3 patients from 18yo to 80yo
* Undergoing unilateral oncologic breast surgery under PVBs

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient refusal or inability to consent
* Allergy to medication used in the trial
* Pregnant or breastfeeding women
* Low body weight (under 50 kg)
* BMI over 40
* Moderate to severe COPD or other moderate to severe respiratory condition
* Contraindications to locoregional anesthesia: Infection at the site of blocks, coagulopathy, anatomic distorsion, neuropathy.
